title: model-loading-weights-shard-breadcrumbs-priya-desai
content:
Context:
I was debugging a recurring failure when loading the 70B model on Dedicated cluster node pool (g5.12x). The runtime crashes during initial checkpoint load (~4-7% into model load) with different errors depending on retry attempts. This doc collects commands tried, error snippets, hypotheses, and next steps breadcrumbs for triage and handoff.

Environment:
- Runtime: redwood-serving v2.13.1 (container image sha: a1b2c3d)
- Node: g5.12x, Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 5.15
- Python: 3.10.12, torch 2.2.0, safetensors 0.4.0, transformers 4.30.0
- Checkpoint source: S3 (internal bucket: s3://redwood-models/70b/safetensors-sharded/), 10 shards (00000-of-00010 .. 00009-of-00010) + manifest.json
- Download mechanism: internal downloader using range requests + concurrent workers (default 8) writing shards to /var/lib/redwood/models/<model-id>

Failure timeline (high level):
- 2024-11-01: First report from canary: load failure during weights mapping, node restarts.
- 2024-11-02: Repro locally on dev node with same container image. Intermittent: sometimes load succeeds if we re-run without cleaning disk.
- 2024-11-03: Started detailed breadcrumb capture (this doc).

Commands & outputs tried (in order):
1) Manual download (single shard) to validate object integrity:
   aws s3 cp s3://redwood-models/70b/safetensors-sharded/pytorch_model-00003-of-00010.safetensors ./pytorch_model-00003-of-00010.safetensors
   # exit code 0; file size: 1,024,000,512 bytes
   sha256sum ./pytorch_model-00003-of-00010.safetensors
   -> 7f8c9f2e4b...  (compared to manifest: 7f8c9f2e4b...)  OK

2) Run runtime load with verbose logging (RUNTIME_DEBUG=1):
   ./start-runtime.sh --model-id 70b-test
   Logs show: "Loading shard 00003-of-00010" then "EOFError: Unexpected end of file while mapping weights"
   Stack (snippet):
     File "/opt/redwood/loader.py", line 214, in _map_shard
       mm = memory_map(file_path)
     File "/opt/redwood/utils/io.py", line 47, in memory_map
       raise EOFError(f'file truncated: {file_path}')

   Note: repeating the same run sometimes yields "ValueError: checksum mismatch for shard 00003-of-00010" instead.

3) Check disk space & inode exhaustion:
   df -h -> plenty of space (200G free)
   df -i -> inodes OK
   dmesg -> no OOM or kernel I/O errors

4) Re-run downloader with single-threaded mode (concurrency=1):
   Modified downloader config and restarted. Result: load completes ~60% of the time. When it fails, error often is EOFError again but on different shard number.

5) Verified manifest and shard ordering:
   cat manifest.json -> confirms 10 shards with sizes and sha256 sums
   Parsed manifest locally and compared checksums for all 10 shards -> all match on repeated downloads

6) Induced partial download by interrupting downloader (ctrl-c) to reproduce truncated shard behavior:
   Observation: runtime error message exactly matches when shard file is truncated. This indicates loader does not detect incomplete files robustly if file exists.

7) Attempted atomic write fix locally: write to tmp + rename after full download -> resolved intermittent EOFError locally. But production downloader already uses atomic rename; still see failures in prod.

8) Pulled raw HTTP logs from S3 gateway: noticed occasional 200 responses with shorter content-length header than actual partial file content (suspect proxy bug or connection reset with 200).

9) Reproduced with gsutil against GCS copy (we also mirrored to gcs://redwood-models/70b/): behavior similar, but less frequent.

10) Checked network flaps metrics for the node pool -> increased retransmits on that AZ during the observed window.

Error snippets collected:
- EOFError: file truncated: /var/lib/redwood/models/70b/pytorch_model-00003-of-00010.safetensors
- ValueError: checksum mismatch for shard 00003-of-00010 (expected 7f8c9..., got 1a2b3...)
- OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device (only once; coincided with other disk activity)
- AssertionError: shard count mismatch: found 9 files, manifest expects 10

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Transient network/proxy issues cause partial downloads that sometimes get committed (race with rename logic), leading to EOFError or checksum mismatch. Explains intermittent nature and correlation with AZ network metrics.
2) Downloader concurrency bug: multiple workers writing same target path or renaming while another thread reads; atomicity assumptions broken under load. Single-threaded downloads reduce failure rate, supporting this.
3) Manifest or shard naming inconsistency: rare, but observed assertion where loader reported 9 files. Could be deletion/cleanup race with garbage collector.
4) Corrupt upload for a specific shard: less likely because manual downloads repeatedly matched manifest checksum.
5) Incompatible checkpoint format or loader bug in memory mapping for safetensors, but widespread success elsewhere argues against it.

What I tried to mitigate (and results):
- Force single-threaded downloads -> big improvement (success ~60-70%)
- Add pre-download size+sha256 validation step: download to tmp, verify size & sha256, then rename -> fixes EOF/checksum when done locally
- Added retry logic on checksum mismatch with exponential backoff -> reduces impact but increases startup time
- Temporarily increased downloader logging and added file write synchronization primitives -> observed fewer races in logs but still see occasional corrupted/partial writes
- Mirrored model to GCS and updated downloader to prefer GCS for this model -> reduced failure rate (GCS more stable for this AZ)

Open questions / next steps for handoff:
- Can infra confirm network packet retransmit spikes / proxy errors for the AZ/time windows? (cc: SRE)
- We should audit downloader code path for any non-atomic file write patterns under high concurrency. I suspect a rename/torrent style commit race when worker A thinks file is complete but worker B still writing a different shard with same tmp name (we use tmp pattern: <shard>.tmp).
- Add robust verification in the runtime loader: if checksum mismatch or EOF on memory map, attempt to re-download shard before failing the entire model load. This will buy resilience and avoid full restart.
- Consider increasing downloader default concurrency timeout and reducing parallelism for large sharded models (>= 10 shards).
- Add metrics/alerting on number of checksum mismatches per model load to detect regressions earlier.

Immediate short-term remediation applied today (2024-11-08):
- Switched canary to use GCS mirror for 70B model.
- Deployed a small downloader patch (v0.27.3) that:
  * writes to unique tmp per worker (tmp name includes worker id + pid)
  * validates size + sha256 before rename
  * retries up to 3 times on network errors
  Observed: canary passed 12/12 loads in 2 hours after deploy.

Notes for the eng-sre handoff:
- Relevant infra ticket: JIRA-INF-3421 (linked above)
- Logs + sample corrupted shard saved under /var/log/redwood/incident/70b/ (see github PR for collector script)
- If SRE finds proxy/gateway issues, coordinating a re-run of downloader over affected time window to re-validate shard integrity is recommended.

Appendix - quick reproduction steps:
1) On dev node with container image a1b2c3d:
   export MODEL_DIR=/tmp/70b-test; rm -rf $MODEL_DIR; mkdir -p $MODEL_DIR
   # start internal downloader with concurrency=8 to the model dir
   python -m redwood.downloader --source s3://redwood-models/70b/safetensors-sharded/ --dest $MODEL_DIR --concurrency 8
2) Start runtime: ./start-runtime.sh --model-dir $MODEL_DIR --model-id 70b-test
3) Watch logs for EOFError or checksum mismatch. If observed, try re-running downloader with --concurrency 1 and verify checksums.

Contacts / owners for follow-up:
- Priya Desai (me) - primary triage
- Jordan Wu - downloader code owner
- Maya Chen - loader/mmap owner
- SRE oncall (cc in JIRA)

Status: draft; saving breadcrumbs here for handoff. Will convert to a more formal postmortem if SRE confirms infra cause or if we discover a persistent downloader bug.

-- end of notes --
